_meta.description: Illustration provenance manifest. Each entry binds a deterministic asset (TikZ / SVG / matplotlib redraw) to a source LaTeX block AND a human-authored direction prompt via cryptographic hashes. Image generation models MAY be used during draft exploration; the certificate trusts only the deterministic redraw. Edits to the source block OR the direction invalidate the asset's certificate until re-authored.
_meta.claim_scope_default: schematic illustration only; not empirical evidence
_meta.design_v2_change: Removed the text-model spec layer (was a tool used as a judge: it interpreted what the human already knew, removing the human's ability to inject 'compare to X' direction). v2 takes the human direction prompt directly. Source LaTeX hash anchors provenance; direction hash records exploration intent; image model produces draft; deterministic redraw is what ships.

staging_vs_refine.tex.source_excerpt: \textbf{Constitutional AI.} Critique-revision ... is the geometric solution: one principle per revision avoids diagonal cost. Our bound explains why: sequential satisfaction sidesteps the sqrt(k/(1-rho(k-1))) penalty.
staging_vs_refine.tex.direction_prompt:
3-panel side-by-side comparison of three control protocols on the same multi-constraint problem: (a) Self-Refine, (b) Decompose, (c) Staged.

Panel (a) Self-Refine: vertical chain of red-tinted boxes — generate -> output y_t -> critique -> revise — with a dashed red arrow looping back from "revise" to "output y_t" labeled "iterate". Caption: "Loops around the output, not the constraint structure". Cost annotation: "640 tokens (Tab.~ref{tab:baselines})".

Panel (b) Decompose: purple-tinted boxes — top "split: k -> k subproblems" forks down to three sub-boxes "sub C_1", "sub C_2", "... sub C_k" which converge into "combine". Caption: "Each subproblem has effective k=1; combine inherits coupling". Cost annotation: "parallel; coupling cost on combine".

Panel (c) Staged: vertical chain of blue-tinted boxes — z^(0) start -> satisfy C_1 -> anchor z^(1) -> satisfy C_2 -> anchor z^(2) ... Caption: "One constraint per step; sidesteps sqrt(k/(1-rho(k-1)))". Cost annotation: "512 tokens; geometric router 384".

Bottom summary line spanning all three panels: "Self-Refine addresses CAPABILITY VARIANCE; Staged addresses CONSTRAINT STRUCTURE; Decompose reduces effective k."

Style: minimal, sans-serif labels, rounded rectangles, color-tinted fills (red / purple / blue per panel), arrows for flow. White background.
staging_vs_refine.tex.claim_scope: schematic illustration only; not empirical evidence. Three-protocol comparison (Self-Refine, Decompose, Staged) of the same multi-constraint problem, addressing reviewer concern about distinguishing staging from iterative refinement. Token counts cite Table tab:baselines.
staging_vs_refine.tex.notes: First illustration authored under the v2 (no-spec-model) schema. Direction prompt captures the human's exploration intent (3-panel comparison with specific token costs and per-panel captions). Image draft will be regenerated with this direction; the deterministic TikZ asset is already authored.

algorithm1_routing.tex.source_excerpt: \begin{algorithm}[t] \caption{Regime-Based Routing: One-Shot, Stage, or Decompose, Decided Before Generation} \label{alg:routing} ...
algorithm1_routing.tex.direction_prompt: Vertical decision tree of Algorithm 1 routing logic. Layers top to bottom: (1) Input box "prompt P, budget T, encoder Phi". (2) Compute box "Parse constraints C_1 ... C_k from P". (3) Two parallel compute boxes side by side: "Compute rho-hat = max cos(Phi(C_i), Phi(C_j))" and "Estimate delta = L-hat * T". (4) Compute box "Screened cost delta-min-hat = (tau/m) sqrt(k / (1 - rho-hat (k-1)))". (5) Decision box (orange) "Route on rho-hat and delta/delta-min-hat". (6) Three terminal boxes side by side: One-Shot (green) condition "rho-hat < 0.15 OR delta/delta-min-hat > 2"; Staged (blue) condition "rho-hat < 0.5 AND delta/delta-min-hat > 1.2"; Decompose-First (purple) condition "else: rho-hat >= 0.5". Conditions printed in small font next to each terminal arrow. Arrows from parallel compute boxes converge into the screened cost. Style: minimal, sans-serif, rounded boxes, light-tinted fills.
algorithm1_routing.tex.claim_scope: schematic illustration only; not empirical evidence. Decision-tree shape derived under v1 schema (text-model + image-model); the deterministic TikZ asset implements the tree with paper-accurate conditions (lines 6-12 of Algorithm 1).
algorithm1_routing.tex.notes: Migrated from v1 schema. The original draft and final asset were produced when a text-model spec layer existed; the direction_prompt above reverse-engineers what a human direction would have said. Original spec retained at supplementary/illustrations/algorithm1_routing_spec.md for historical record.

interface_assumption.tex.source_excerpt: \fbox{\begin{minipage}...Interface Assumption (text-in, text-out, frozen encoder, deterministic verifier; High-Probability Lipschitz)...$\|x_T - x_0\|_2 \le LT$...The $\varepsilon$-mass (11%) is the pivot regime...
interface_assumption.tex.direction_prompt: Horizontal dataflow with 5 boxes: Prompt P (text in) -> Frozen encoder Phi (no internals accessed) -> Decoder (per-token displacement <= L) -> Response y (text out) -> Verifier (deterministic pass/fail). Above the Decoder, an annotation in dark orange: "epsilon-mass (epsilon-hat <= 0.11): pivot regime, detected mid-generation, rerouted." Below the Decoder, an annotation: "Triangle inequality over T tokens: ||x_T - x_0||_2 <= L T." Style: minimal, sans-serif, rounded boxes with light fill (gray for encoder, white for I/O, orange for decoder, blue for verifier). Arrows between boxes; dashed connector arrows from annotations to the Decoder.
interface_assumption.tex.claim_scope: schematic illustration only; not empirical evidence. Reviewer aid; the dataflow it depicts (text -> frozen encoder -> bounded per-token displacement -> deterministic verifier) is exactly what the source LaTeX block at main.tex:253-257 asserts in prose.
interface_assumption.tex.notes: First illustration in the framework. Originally authored without a draft model (hand-authored TikZ from the human's understanding of the source); migrated to v2 schema by recording the direction the human had in mind. Demonstrates that draft_model is OPTIONAL — the framework supports hand-authored illustrations alongside image-model-drafted ones, with the same provenance binding.
